options.text: Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients (SRTR)
Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Physician Fee Schedule
FDA MedWatch adverse event database only
National Marrow Donor Program registry

explanation.rationale_correct: The SRTR contains current and past information about the full continuum of transplant activity. Data are collected by the OPTN from hospitals and OPOs and used for policy development, program analysis, and outcome reporting.

rationale_incorrect.B: CMS fee schedules govern reimbursement, not the national transplant outcomes registry described in OPTN/SRTR references.
rationale_incorrect.C: FDA MedWatch is a drug and device adverse-event system, not the primary national transplant outcomes registry.
rationale_incorrect.D: The National Marrow Donor Program registry supports hematopoietic cell transplantation, not the solid-organ SRTR database.

stem: You are the transplant coordinator coordinating follow-up labs before the surgeon clinic. A 39-year-old solid-organ transplant patient is the focus of today's interaction. They should wait one week before reporting missed doses

rationale_incorrect.D: Missed doses during illness require timely team contact, not delayed reporting.

stem: You are the transplant coordinator coordinating follow-up labs before the surgeon clinic. A 39-year-old solid-organ transplant patient is the focus of today's interaction. It has been several weeks since transplant. Vital signs are stable, but the clinical picture still warrants coordinator input. What counseling is MOST accurate?

options.text: Diabetes may develop in up to about half of recipients within the first three months
Diabetes never occurs after transplantation because immunosuppression prevents it
Diabetes appears only after ten years and never in the first year
Post-transplant diabetes requires no monitoring because it cannot affect long-term outcomes

explanation.rationale_correct: Diabetes after transplantation may occur in up to 50% of solid organ transplant recipients within the first three months and worsens long-term outcomes, requiring monitoring and management.

rationale_incorrect.B: Immunosuppression, including corticosteroids and CNIs, contributes to post-transplant diabetes rather than preventing it.
rationale_incorrect.C: Post-transplant diabetes is common in the early post-transplant period, not exclusively after a decade.
rationale_incorrect.D: Post-transplant diabetes decreases quality of life and worsens long-term outcomes, so monitoring is required.

stem: You are updating central venous line (CVL) infection protocols. Attendees will apply the material when fielding recipient calls. Evaluate the following statements:
